WRONG Q1: What does the performance analysis say? right 0missed 4wrong 1of 4 GT
Right — GT sentence found (0)
Missed — GT sentence not found (4)
  • Detectors trained on one generator perform well on generators with similar artifacts but poorly on others.
    GT · performance.analysis
  • Diffusion models leave very different forensic traces: GLIDE, Latent Diffusion and Stable Diffusion show clear spectral peaks similar to GANs, while ADM and DALL·E 2 show much weaker ones and are the hardest to detect.
    GT · performance.analysis

WRONG Q15: What are the main takeaways about this model? right 0missed 9wrong 1of 9 GT
Right — GT sentence found (0)
Missed — GT sentence not found (9)
  • A convolutional detector that classifies images as real or fully synthetic.
    GT · overview.description
  • Detectors trained on one generator perform well on generators with similar artifacts but poorly on others.
    GT · performance.analysis
  • Diffusion models leave very different forensic traces: GLIDE, Latent Diffusion and Stable Diffusion show clear spectral peaks similar to GANs, while ADM and DALL·E 2 show much weaker ones and are the hardest to detect.
    GT · performance.analysis
  • Fusing detectors trained on different generators and calibrating the threshold on a few samples substantially improves accuracy, although images whose artifacts differ strongly from those seen in training remain difficult to detect.
    GT · performance.analysis
  • In the resized and compressed setting, AUC often remains acceptable on unseen generators, but accuracy at a fixed threshold drops close to chance.
    GT · performance.analysis
  • It is optimized for images generated by the Ablated Diffusion Model (ADM) and similar diffusion architectures.
    GT · overview.description
  • It may also flag images from other generative models, but performance outside the ADM family is not guaranteed.
    GT · overview.description
  • The architecture is a ResNet-50 variant with an initial residual-extraction layer and no downsampling in the first layer, which helps preserve the subtle high-frequency traces left by the generation process.
    GT · overview.description
  • The model is trained from scratch on ADM images with strong augmentation (blurring, JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, geometric transformations, cut-out, and brightness and contrast changes) to make it more robust to the processing images undergo on social networks.
    GT · overview.description
Wrong — predicted but not in GT (1)

  • For every patch, a frozen DINOv2-L/14 vision encoder represents the patch together with its low- and high-frequency components, and the similarity between these representations (spectral reconstruction similarity) is used as evidence, read in the context of the patch content (spectral context vector).
    GT · overview.description
  • Spectral context attention then weighs the patches and combines them into one image-level score between 0 (real) and 1 (AI-generated).
    GT · overview.description
  • What differs from the original SPAI: the masked-spectral-learning ViT-B/16 backbone is replaced by DINOv2-L/14, and the model is trained on lab-generated (LDM) and in-the-wild (TWIGMA) AI images, with real images from COCO, LSUN and OpenImages, using strong augmentations.
    GT · overview.description

  • Design faults: the model depends on subtle low-level traces that compression, resizing and re-capture remove; it gives a single image-level score without localisation; authentic images that share traits with generated ones (digital art, heavy editing, upscaling) can be flagged; the score is not calibrated.
    GT · safety.risks
  • Environmental threats: new generators and AI editing tools appear continuously, so accuracy decays over time; deliberate post-processing or adversarial perturbations can be used to evade detection; platforms change how they process images.
    GT · safety.risks
  • ITW-SPAI is not the public SPAI release: it uses a DINOv2-L/14 backbone instead of SPAI's masked-spectral-learning ViT-B/16, and different training data, so results for the public SPAI weights do not apply to it, and vice versa.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • It is a research model deployed to support verification and has not been validated for forensic or legal use.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • Only fully AI-generated and real images were considered; behaviour on partially edited or AI-enhanced real photos is unknown.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • Possible consequences: synthetic images accepted as authentic and spread as disinformation; authentic images wrongly discredited; misplaced trust in automated verdicts.
    GT · safety.risks
  • Technical faults: pipelines that downscale, re-encode or screenshot images before submission degrade results; very small images provide little evidence; service errors return an error report instead of a score.
    GT · safety.risks
  • The ITW-SPAI weights are not public, so third parties cannot reproduce its results exactly.
    GT · safety.caveats

WRONG Q1: Is this model safe? right 0missed 13wrong 3of 13 GT
Right — GT sentence found (0)
Missed — GT sentence not found (13)
  • Caveats: the score is not a calibrated probability; the model does not localise manipulations; it is not designed for partially edited images or for derivative copies such as screenshots and re-photographed or printed images; and its training data predate generators released after early 2023.
    GT · overview.description
  • Design faults: the model depends on subtle low-level traces that compression, resizing and re-capture remove; it gives a single image-level score without localisation; authentic images that share traits with generated ones (digital art, heavy editing, upscaling) can be flagged; the score is not calibrated.
    GT · safety.risks
  • Environmental threats: new generators and AI editing tools appear continuously, so accuracy decays over time; deliberate post-processing or adversarial perturbations can be used to evade detection; platforms change how they process images.
    GT · safety.risks
  • False negatives can lend credibility to synthetic images used for disinformation, impersonation or fraud.
    GT · safety.ethics
  • False positives can damage the credibility of genuine photographs, of their authors and of the outlets that publish them, and can be used to dismiss real documentation of events as fake.
    GT · safety.ethics
  • It is a research model deployed to support verification and has not been validated for forensic or legal use.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • No formal fairness criterion was defined, applied or measured during development.
    GT · safety.fairness
  • Performance across demographic groups (e.g. skin tone, gender, age) has not been evaluated.
    GT · performance.bias
  • Possible consequences: synthetic images accepted as authentic and spread as disinformation; authentic images wrongly discredited; misplaced trust in automated verdicts.
    GT · safety.risks
  • Recommended mitigations: keep a human expert in charge of every decision; report the evidence level rather than a binary verdict; corroborate with independent evidence such as provenance checks, reverse image search and detectors from other families; analyse the original file; explain the model's limits whenever its output is cited in public.
    GT · safety.ethics
  • Robustness to adversarial attacks has not been evaluated.
    GT · safety.security
  • Technical faults: pipelines that downscale, re-encode or screenshot images before submission degrade results; very small images provide little evidence; service errors return an error report instead of a score.
    GT · safety.risks
  • The model and the service are not certified for cybersecurity, and no compliance with specific security standards is reported.
    GT · safety.security

Right — GT sentence found (0)
Missed — GT sentence not found (15)
  • Caveats: the score is not a calibrated probability; the model does not localise manipulations; it is not designed for partially edited images or for derivative copies such as screenshots and re-photographed or printed images; and its training data predate generators released after early 2023.
    GT · overview.description
  • Design faults: the model depends on subtle low-level traces that compression, resizing and re-capture remove; it gives a single image-level score without localisation; authentic images that share traits with generated ones (digital art, heavy editing, upscaling) can be flagged; the score is not calibrated.
    GT · safety.risks
  • Environmental threats: new generators and AI editing tools appear continuously, so accuracy decays over time; deliberate post-processing or adversarial perturbations can be used to evade detection; platforms change how they process images.
    GT · safety.risks
  • ITW-SPAI is not the public SPAI release: it uses a DINOv2-L/14 backbone instead of SPAI's masked-spectral-learning ViT-B/16, and different training data, so results for the public SPAI weights do not apply to it, and vice versa.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • It is a research model deployed to support verification and has not been validated for forensic or legal use.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • Newer generators may be missed.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • Only fully AI-generated and real images were considered; behaviour on partially edited or AI-enhanced real photos is unknown.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • Possible consequences: synthetic images accepted as authentic and spread as disinformation; authentic images wrongly discredited; misplaced trust in automated verdicts.
    GT · safety.risks
  • Processing history: recompression, downscaling, cropping, filters and repeated re-sharing weaken or erase the low-level traces the model relies on.
    GT · use.factors
  • Recommended mitigations: keep a human expert in charge of every decision; report the evidence level rather than a binary verdict; corroborate with independent evidence such as provenance checks, reverse image search and detectors from other families; analyse the original file; explain the model's limits whenever its output is cited in public.
    GT · safety.ethics
  • Serving as the sole basis for publishing a verdict, for legal or disciplinary decisions, or for accusations against individuals.
    GT · use.out_of_scope_use
  • Technical faults: pipelines that downscale, re-encode or screenshot images before submission degrade results; very small images provide little evidence; service errors return an error report instead of a score.
    GT · safety.risks
  • The ITW-SPAI weights are not public, so third parties cannot reproduce its results exactly.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • The original SPAI paper reports failures on derivative AI images (screenshots, photos of screens, printed copies) whose traces were destroyed; ITW-SPAI has not been evaluated on such images and likely shares this limitation.
    GT · safety.caveats
  • Treating a low score as proof that an image is authentic, or a high score as proof that it is AI-generated.
    GT · use.out_of_scope_use
